q: אדם בן 82 תלוי במטפלת לצרכיו הבסיסיים. תועד שהמטפלת הכתה אותו ושנמנעה באופן מתמשך מאספקת מזון וטיפול בהיגיינה. איזה שילוב סוגי פגיעה מתואר לפי נוהל משרד הבריאות?
o: התעמרות נפשית והתעמרות כלכלית
התעמרות פיזית והזנחת צרכים בסיסיים
התעמרות כלכלית והזנחת צרכים בסיסיים
התעמרות פיזית והתעמרות כלכלית
explanation:
מכות הן פגיעה ישירה בגוף. מניעת מזון והזנחת היגיינה לאורך זמן הן כשל בטיפול הבסיסי באדם תלוי. **התעמרות פיזית והזנחת צרכים בסיסיים**.

**א. התעמרות נפשית והתעמרות כלכלית.** אין תיאור של שימוש בלתי מורשה ברכוש.
**ב. התעמרות פיזית והזנחת צרכים בסיסיים.** השילוב מכסה את המעשה האלים ואת המחדל המתמשך.
**ג. התעמרות כלכלית והזנחת צרכים בסיסיים.** הרכיב הגופני אינו ניצול כספי.
**ד. התעמרות פיזית והתעמרות כלכלית.** האפשרות אינה מסבירה את החסך במזון ובהיגיינה.

אסמכתא · נוהל טיפול בזקנים נפגעי התעמרות, עמ׳ 4.
ref: משרד הבריאות, חוזר המנהל הכללי 22/03: נוהל טיפול בזקנים נפגעי התעמרות

q: A patient develops severe symptomatic hyponatremia after surgery. Which management principle is consistent with Hazzard?
o: Start prompt treatment guided by cause and volume status, with sodium monitoring
Complete the investigation of the cause before starting treatment for hyponatremia
Base treatment on the sodium concentration without evaluating the patient’s volume status
Treat the sodium abnormality and defer repeat sodium measurements until recovery
explanation:
Severe neurologic manifestations of hypotonic hyponatremia, such as seizures or markedly reduced consciousness, can reflect cerebral edema. **Start monitored IV 3% hypertonic saline promptly when these manifestations are present**, alongside stabilization, frequent sodium measurements and investigation of the perioperative cause.

**A. Treat promptly and monitor.** Aim for an initial small rise sufficient to relieve dangerous symptoms, then control further correction. Determine volume status and stop contributing drugs or fluids as appropriate.
**B. Complete the investigation first.** Delaying emergency treatment can prolong cerebral edema. Diagnostic assessment can proceed during stabilization.
**C. Use the sodium concentration alone.** Neurologic severity guides immediate treatment. Volume status, timing and cause guide subsequent fluid management.
**D. Wait until recovery to recheck sodium.** Overly rapid correction can produce osmotic demyelination. Repeat measurements are essential during treatment.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 587. European clinical practice guideline on hyponatraemia, section 7.1, PMID 24569125.
ref: Hazzard Ch 39 — SYSTEMS PHYSIOLOGY OF AGING AND SELECTED DISORDERS OF HOMEOSTASIS

q: A 78-year-old man with severe COPD (FEV1 35% predicted) presents with acute dyspnea and confusion. His daughter reports two days of memory difficulty and failure to recognize her this morning. His home medications include tiotropium, budesonide/formoterol, and lorazepam 0.5 mg three times daily, recently started for anxiety. Arterial blood gases show pH 7.32, pCO2 58, and pO2 65 on 2 L/min by nasal cannula. Chest radiography shows hyperinflation without infiltrates, and examination reveals asterixis. Medication review focuses on a possible benzodiazepine contribution. Which effect described by Hazzard is relevant?
o: Increased ventilatory control and increased aspiration risk
Decreased ventilatory control and increased aspiration risk
Decreased ventilatory control and decreased aspiration risk
Increased ventilatory control and decreased aspiration risk
explanation:
Ventilatory control drives the response to a rising CO₂ level. A sedative can blunt that response and impair protective airway reflexes.
**Lorazepam can decrease ventilatory control and increase aspiration risk.**

**A. Increased drive and increased aspiration.** The aspiration concern is plausible, but a benzodiazepine depresses rather than stimulates ventilatory drive.
**B. Decreased drive and increased aspiration.** New sedation can aggravate CO₂ retention and impair airway protection. The respiratory acidosis also requires direct assessment and treatment.
**C. Decreased drive and decreased aspiration.** The direction of the aspiration effect is reversed.
**D. Increased drive and decreased aspiration.** Neither effect describes the respiratory risks of adding lorazepam in this setting.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 1247.
ref: Hazzard Ch 81 — CHRONIC OBSTRUCTIVE PULMONARY DISEASE

q: A 79-year-old nursing-home resident with advanced Parkinson disease and recurrent UTIs has worsening constipation despite lactulose 30 mL daily. She has had no bowel movement for five days and reports abdominal pain. Examination shows abdominal distension and a large, firm rectal fecal impaction. She takes carbidopa/levodopa, oxybutynin 5 mg twice daily, and prophylactic trimethoprim; creatinine clearance is 35 mL/min. Before inserting rectal enemas or suppositories, what does Hazzard recommend for the firm impaction?
o: Perform manual evacuation with local anesthetic gel for discomfort
Insert phosphate enemas before attempting manual evacuation
Defer manual evacuation until a course of oral PEG is complete
Insert bisacodyl suppositories before attempting manual evacuation
explanation:
A large hard mass in the rectum creates a physical barrier even when oral laxatives have been taken. Parkinson disease and oxybutynin can both predispose to recurrence.
**Remove the firm impaction gently before inserting an enema or suppository.**

**A. Manual evacuation with anesthetic gel.** This relieves the distal obstruction and reduces discomfort when gel is needed.
**B. Phosphate enema first.** An impacted plug impedes insertion. Renal impairment adds risk from absorbed phosphate.
**C. Wait for oral PEG.** PEG can help further clearance and maintenance, but waiting leaves the accessible painful mass in place.
**D. Bisacodyl suppository first.** It stimulates evacuation once the outlet is clear and does not remove a large firm plug directly.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 1376, 1378, Table 87-11.

q: A 72-year-old man with newly diagnosed metastatic pancreatic cancer started sustained-release morphine 30 mg twice daily for pain. Two weeks later, pain is controlled, but he has had no bowel movement for six days despite docusate 200 mg twice daily. Examination shows mild abdominal distention and a moderate amount of stool in the rectal vault. His goals include maintaining quality of life and activity. Which change is supported for treating his opioid-related constipation?
o: Add senna as an active stimulant laxative
Continue docusate as the principal maintenance laxative
Add magnesium citrate as the regular maintenance laxative
Use soapsuds enemas as the regular bowel regimen
explanation:
Morphine slows gut propulsion and can cause constipation even when analgesia is satisfactory. Docusate alone has little laxative effect.
**Add senna, an active stimulant laxative, after assessing the retained stool.**

**A. Senna.** Its propulsive effect addresses opioid-related slowing and can help preserve comfort while analgesia continues.
**B. Docusate as principal treatment.** The current regimen has failed, and simply softening stool does little to correct slow propulsion.
**C. Magnesium citrate.** Rapid catharsis and fluid loss make it a poor regular regimen for an older patient.
**D. Regular soapsuds enemas.** Repeated rectal irrigation can irritate the mucosa and is unnecessarily burdensome for maintenance.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 1372–1374, 1376–1378.

q: An older woman takes gabapentin and has a creatinine clearance of 42 mL/min. Which treatment adjustment matches the 2023 AGS Beers Criteria?
o: Increase the dose to compensate for impaired kidney function
Reduce the dose because of central nervous system adverse effects
Maintain the dose and substitute liver-function monitoring for renal adjustment
Maintain the dose and substitute blood-count monitoring for renal adjustment
explanation:
The kidneys eliminate gabapentin, so reduced filtration can prolong exposure and cause central adverse effects.

**Reduce gabapentin at a creatinine clearance of 42 mL/min.** This falls below the 60 mL/min renal dosing threshold.

**A. Increase for renal impairment.** Slower elimination favors accumulation with a higher dose.
**B. Reduce for CNS effects.** Adjusting the regimen downward helps limit drowsiness, confusion, and other central effects.
**C. Use liver tests instead.** Liver tests do not measure the renal elimination problem or prevent drug accumulation.
**D. Use blood counts instead.** Checking for hematologic changes cannot replace renal dose adjustment.

Reference · 2023 AGS Beers Criteria, p. 2073.

q: A 79-year-old man with locally advanced prostate cancer has received leuprolide for 18 months. He reports progressive fatigue, poor appetite, and loss of interest in woodworking. His PHQ-9 score is 14; his wife died 8 months ago. Testosterone is below 20 ng/dL and creatinine clearance is 44 mL/min. If depression is confirmed after excluding other causes, which drug belongs to the first-line group described in Hazzard's cancer chapter?
o: Sertraline as initial antidepressant treatment
Nortriptyline as initial antidepressant treatment
Bupropion as initial antidepressant treatment
Venlafaxine as initial antidepressant treatment
explanation:
Fatigue and poor appetite during cancer treatment have several potential causes, including depression. **Once depression is confirmed, sertraline is a first-line selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor.**

**A. Sertraline** — An SSRI is an appropriate initial medication in this framework. Follow mood, tolerability and function after starting it.
**B. Nortriptyline** — This tricyclic is a later-line choice. Anticholinergic and cardiovascular effects are important in older patients.
**C. Bupropion** — This alternative can be considered when the initial SSRI is unsuitable or ineffective.
**D. Venlafaxine** — A serotonin-norepinephrine reuptake inhibitor can be used later. It is outside the first-line class asked for here.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 1392, Anxiety and depression.
label: Source: Hazzard 8e (marked) · p. 1392, Anxiety and depression

q: An 84-year-old man with early-stage non-small-cell lung cancer is medically inoperable because of severe lung disease. The team proposes stereotactic body radiotherapy (SBRT). Which description captures its technical advantage over conventional radiation in Hazzard?
o: Radiation to a broad volume in small doses over a prolonged treatment course
Focused, ablative radiation doses to the lung tumor over a few fractions
Low-dose radiation to the whole body to control microscopic sites of disease
Radiation to a broad thoracic field in small doses over several weeks
explanation:
Stereotactic body radiotherapy is a local ablative treatment for medically inoperable early-stage lung cancer. **Precisely focused high doses over a few fractions** distinguish it from conventional fractionation.

**A. Broad field, prolonged course.** Conventional small fractions over many visits do not describe stereotactic targeting.
**B. Focused ablative fractions.** The selected target receives a high dose while limiting exposure of surrounding lung.
**C. Low-dose whole-body treatment.** SBRT concentrates treatment at the primary tumor rather than treating circulating or distant disease.
**D. Broad thoracic field.** A large field over several weeks lacks the target precision and short schedule described here.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 1425.

q: An 80-year-old man with myelodysplastic syndrome has transfusion-related iron overload. Before deciding about iron chelation, the team assesses disease risk, continuing transfusion needs, and expected survival. Which combination matches the Hazzard recommendation for initiating chelation?
o: Higher-risk MDS, ongoing transfusion dependence, expected survival under one year
Lower-risk MDS, ongoing transfusion dependence, expected survival over one year
Lower-risk MDS, ongoing transfusion dependence, expected survival under one year
Lower-risk MDS, transfusions no longer needed, expected survival over one year
explanation:
Repeated red-cell transfusions deliver iron that accumulates over time. **Consider chelation for transfusional iron overload in lower-risk MDS with continuing transfusion dependence and expected survival longer than one year.**

**A. Higher risk, survival under one year** — Rapid disease progression and a short time horizon reduce the opportunity to benefit from removal of accumulated iron.
**B. Lower risk, continuing transfusions, survival over one year** — Continuing exposure and sufficient expected survival make chronic iron accumulation clinically relevant.
**C. Lower risk, survival under one year** — The patient has ongoing exposure but lacks the expected survival interval specified for this approach.
**D. Lower risk, transfusions stopped** — Once transfusions stop, the continuing iron load that favors initiating chelation in transfusion-dependent MDS is absent. Previously accumulated iron still warrants individual assessment.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 1485.
ref: Hazzard Ch 95 — HEMATOLOGIC MALIGNANCIES (LEUKEMIA/LYMPHOMA) AND PLASMA CELL DISORDERS

q: A 77-year-old woman is hospitalized with community-acquired pneumonia and is receiving ceftriaxone. Legionella infection cannot be excluded, and she has no contraindication to a macrolide. Which antibiotic plan agrees with Hazzard while investigations continue?
o: Add azithromycin as a single 500 mg dose alongside ceftriaxone.
Use amoxicillin-clavulanate instead of combining a beta-lactam antibiotic with azithromycin.
Withhold ceftriaxone temporarily while waiting for identification of the pathogen.
Add azithromycin 500 mg daily while continuing treatment with ceftriaxone.
explanation:
Legionella is an intracellular cause of pneumonia that beta-lactams do not cover reliably. In this hospitalized woman, **continue ceftriaxone and add azithromycin 500 mg once daily** while investigations continue.

**A. One dose of azithromycin.** A single 500 mg dose starts the regimen. Continued empiric treatment for possible Legionella requires repeat daily dosing.
**B. Substitute amoxicillin-clavulanate.** Clavulanate inhibits some beta-lactamases. It does not give amoxicillin reliable activity against Legionella.
**C. Pause ceftriaxone.** Holding it would interrupt treatment for common bacterial causes such as pneumococcus before the pathogen is known.
**D. Continue ceftriaxone and add daily azithromycin.** The macrolide reaches intracellular Legionella while the beta-lactam maintains coverage for pneumococcus and other common bacterial pathogens.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 1689, Table 105-11.
ref: Hazzard Ch 105 — BACTERIAL PNEUMONIA AND TUBERCULOSIS

q: מה מאפיין Fever of Unknown Origin (FUO) בזקנים בצורה שונה מצעירים?
o: בזקנים FUO מוגדר כבר לאחר שבוע של חום ללא סיבה
בזקנים מעל 50% מהסיבות ל- FUO הן מחלות ממאירות
בזקנים ובצעירים אחת הסיבות השכיחות היא SLE- systemic lupus erythematosus
בזקנים שכיחות גבוהה יותר למחלות אוטואימוניות כסיבה ל- FUO
explanation:
The age-related clue in fever of unknown origin is the distribution of its causes. **Autoimmune disease accounts for a larger share in older adults**, particularly giant cell arteritis and related inflammatory syndromes.

**A. One week of fever is sufficient** — The classic definition includes at least three weeks of fever. The week refers to unsuccessful diagnostic evaluation.
**B. Malignancy exceeds half** — Malignancy accounts for approximately one fifth in the older cohorts summarized.
**C. Lupus is frequent at both ages** — Lupus features in younger adult series and is essentially absent as a cause in the older series described.
**D. Autoimmune causes are relatively more frequent** — Nearly one quarter of cases after 60 were autoimmune in the discussion. Giant cell arteritis can present as fever with few cranial symptoms.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 1675–1676, Table 104-2.
